text_fidelity_a:
My First Thomas & Friends, On-the-Go Train Set This is a fun little train set for toddlers. The current product image is misleading, however, so I've posted photos to show how this nice little set comes. It comes in a handy carry bag with large plastic track pieces and two toys: Thomas the Tank Engine and Harold the Helicopter. Not quite sure why they include a helicopter to roll around a train track, but I suppose he is one of the more popular characters in Thomas' world. Regardless, they are both cute and large enough for a toddler to get his hands on and push around the track.

Thomas and Harold come attached to a piece of cardboard which keeps them in place. Before you go crazy on how to get these off - after a bit of struggling myself, I realized that all you have to do is rotate the plastic tab things that are holding them in place (located on the bottom). Just turn the tabs 90 degrees (doesn't matter which way) to free Thomas and Harold.

You will definitely need to help your put this together as the track pieces have a snug fit. they may loosen with time, however. There are instructions on how to put the track together, though I'm sure you can figure out your own unique layouts as well. The bridge pieces need a special little twist to put them together and remove them, so pay attention to that in the instructions, otherwise the rest simply snap together as you'd expect.

This is a really fun little set with a a nice carry bag to store all the pieces and even take the set with you on adventures. Little ones will love it!
text_fidelity_b: My First Thomas & Friends, On-the-Go Train Set

Colorforms 70th Anniversary Set - The Classic Picture Toy That Sticks Like Magic - Ages 3+ I'm in my 60's and remember Colorforms from when I was a kid. It was and still is in my opinion one of the greatest toys around. Shapes are placed onto a background board and they cling to the board, so the possibilities of creating designs and story scenes are endless.

I do a lot of geometric designing so have a reproduction of the original set, and this anniversary set makes a great addition. The original set is all basic single color shapes. These anniversary sheets (consisting of 4 separate unbound sheets) have those same shapes plus more, and some of these have multiple colors in one shape, with some of those colors being in different patterns and shades as opposed to being all solid colors. There ARE some solid colors, but there are also patterns with stripes, dots, triangles, circles inside of circles, half moons, etc. So this set expands on the designing possibilities with the added dimensions of patterns and color shades. As with the original set, these shapes are peeled off the page they come on and are then placed onto a black background sheet (included) which they cling to until removed.

These sheets are smaller than the original set that comes in a plastic spiral bound book. So if you already have the original in its box, you can just take these sheets from this anniversary set and store in with the original if you don't want to store 2 separate boxes. Overall a nice set that is great as an artsy and learning tool for kids and designing tool for adults who enjoy working with geometric shapes.
text_fidelity_b: Colorforms 70th Anniversary Set - The Classic Picture Toy That Sticks Like Magic - Ages 3+

text_fidelity_a:
ALEX Jr. My Busy Barn I've bought some of the Alex Toys for the children in our family, but this is the first Alex Junior Toy we've owned. Alex Toys are known for their sturdiness, well made enough to pass on to future generations, wonderful educational and imagination values and gorgeous vivid colors. This beautiful barn is no exception with it's sturdiness, educational value and vivid bright colors.

This barn is very sturdy, weighing over 10 pounds and made of both very smooth wood and wood products. You can easily see this lasting for future generations of babies to learn with. There are 6 sides of the barn for learning and play. The 2 sides of the roof are beautifully colored with numbers and corresponding food items- such as the number 8, shows eight ears of corn. One side of the barn has 3 barn doors that when opened, baby can see the animals living inside. The other side of the barn, has a windmill, cloud and sun that, being gears, all turn each other when moved.

The large back of the barn has a moveable tractor, cow and rooster. Baby can move these inside the tracks, so nothing comes loose. The front of the barn includes the most wonderful spinning wood blocks of the alphabet with accompanying pictures. There is a darling owl for the letter O, a cute donkey for the letter D and all the pictures that accompany the letters of the alphabet are not only adorable, but beautifully colored. We have twins in our family and this barn being 6 sided allows them to play on different sides at the same time.

I remember wood alphabet blocks being passed down from one generation to another in our family, but this gorgeous barn will replace that tradition. This barn makes it easy and fun for baby to learn both the alphabet and their numbers at the same time. Our babies love the vivid colors and they love learning that 2 means counting 2 items and that the sound of the letter J sounds like Jam. This is a beautiful barn that your baby will love learning their ABC's and 123's with. It's 5 Star Learning Fun that will last many generations to come.
text_fidelity_b: ALEX Jr. My Busy Barn

Ravensburger Underwater Paradise 9000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - 17807 - Handcrafted Tooling, Durable Blueboard, Every Piece Fits Together Perfectly I know Ravensburger Puzzles are expensive, but worth every penny as they are simply The Best. We have bought them before but never in this huge 9000 piece size. For those not familiar with Ravensburger Puzzles, they are made of the finest sturdy cardboard, hand cut in Germany with such a razor sharp cutter that they leave no cardboard dust and the pieces have an unbelievably tight fit. They have no competitors, as no one comes close to their hand workmanship, bold colors and quality.

The 9000 pieces in this puzzle come in 2 bags- each makes half the puzzle. This makes it so much easier to work on, as we bought 2 pieces of cardboard from our craft store- each a little over 3 feet by 2 feet, to assemble each half on. This half size easily fits on our kitchen table and can be moved easily as well when it's on the cardboard. Included with the 2 puzzle bags is a 3 foot poster of the puzzle to assist you in assembling the beautifully colored pieces. When we were finished with both halves, the full 6 foot 4 inch by 4 1/2 foot puzzle took our breath away! The bold, vivid colors on this large size of all the underwater life looks like a breathtaking work of art just waiting to brighten up a wall in your home.

We decided to put it up on a wall, right behind the children's aquarium- talk about stunning! The only thing we had to decide, is do we use glue to permanently seal it before hanging, or do we seal it tightly in plastic from our local art store, then hang it. The kids said they wanted it in plastic, as they may want to do the puzzle again someday- so it is sealed tightly in plastic against cardboard, framed and hung. If you want this permanently glued, as many people do, all you need to do is buy MasterPieces Puzzle Glue, or any other good puzzle glue and a brush. (I never use the cardboard glue applicators, as the brush is much better). One 5 ounce bottle will seal a 2000 piece puzzle, so you'll need 4 or 5 bottles. You can spread this glue on the front, back or both sides for a permanent bond. It dries clear, so you don't even see the glue.

This 9000 piece high quality Ravensburger Puzzle is worth every cent for the enjoyment of creating a bold, big, beautiful underwater work of art, but what you ultimately gain when you are finished is a gorgeous stunning large wall covering for a bare wall in your home, and that alone is worth the price of these high quality puzzles!
text_fidelity_b: Ravensburger Underwater Paradise 9000 Piece Jigsaw Puzzle for Adults - 17807 - Handcrafted Tooling, Durable Blueboard, Every Piece Fits Together Perfectly

At first I was confused, because I didn't know that My Little Ponies could take human form. I did some research, and the Equestria Girls series was when something was out of balance in the human world, and so Twilight Sparkle, the main pony, jumps through a magic mirror and turns into a human. Her sidekick dragon comes too, and he transforms into a puppy. Somehow they save the day by throwing a pajama party.

I was really impressed with how many points of articulation that the Twilight Sparkle doll has. You'll be able to pose her into whatever position that you want to. She comes with a pajama dress, with bloomers, with two shoes, and with a mask. Spike the puppy doesn't move at all, but he comes with a pajama hat.

As a side note, Twilight Sparkle doesn't have anything to do with the vampire books.

Pros:
+You can pose the doll in a ton of different positions
+High quality clothing
+Her hair is very nice for doll hair
+Fun and exciting

Cons:
-The box doesn't have any instructions or background on why the pony is in human form

text_fidelity_a:
Munchkin® Draw™ Bath Crayons Toddler Bath Toy, 5 Pack OK...so here's the deal with these...
5 stars for how much my 17mo old son LOVES them.
3 stars for how the crayon is constantly coming out of the plastic holder.
Averages to...4 stars.
No one is really addressing a few things, so I will...
these are super bright, amazing, soft crayons that are each a very distinct & different color.
In our particular tub, they color perfectly...but we have a somewhat "satin" finish as opposed to the shiny white finish which is what I imagine is the problem for people who say they don't work. I notice they color fantastically on dry or "damp" tub surfaces...but not as well on truly wet, slick surfaces.
We have a clear silicone table mat with a scene silkscreened on that I sometimes wet the back of and slap on the tub wall so he can color away on it like a coloring book page. Again, the crayons work perfectly when the surface is dry or damp, but can't get grippy enough for the color to stick when it's slick wet.

These crayons do constantly come out of the holders but I just keep pushing them back in. They also push back into the holder because the button is where my son grips the crayons in his tiny hands but when that happens he just moves on to another one, since there are 5.

I put these in to a bag of goodies I gave him for Valentine's Day and ours are still going strong with daily...prolific...color & scribble use on the tub, his tub toys, his picture mat, himself, and Mommy....head to toe. He does lots of "body art" with these, and he enjoys using his scrubby sponge for clean up and erasing his handywork, as much as he does the coloring part!

To me...these babies are worth their weight in gold if you have a budding artist on your hands, the right kind of tub surface, and teach the little virtuoso how to scrub it all clean to start with a fresh canvas! We LOVE...and I mean...LOVE them, and I can't see us ever being without them as my son is pretty much obsessed with all things artistic, and where he is allowed to just cut loose & get messy. These are perfect!

P.S. if you are concerned that teaching them to color on surfaces is a bad or confusing message, which makes perfect sense...I'd say that this is the way to let them be creative & have a blast but teach them that coloring on wall is only for the bathtub and only with these crayons....a concept they will need to learn.

I would recommend getting your first set somewhere that you can return them if they don't work on your tub. Also, get a matte finish silicone baking mat, or matte silicone placemat...wet the back, stick to wall & let them color on that. It works great for us!
text_fidelity_b: Munchkin® Draw™ Bath Crayons Toddler Bath Toy, 5 Pack

WOW! This thing is great! Thousands of bubbles most just under tennis ball size but some smaller. If you use the Gazillion Bubble solution you get beautiful iridescent bubbles that drift a long way before breaking. It works best and the bubble sdrift farther if you can get it up off the ground. A breeze helps too. I set it on the top step of a 3-step ladder and that was perfect. This machine is a bubble solution hog but it couldn't be any less and produce this volume of bubbles. Seems to run maybe 20 minutes or so on a fill and you get about 4 fills from a bottle of the 2 liter Gazillion Bubbles solution. It can make a but of a mess on the ground under the machine so be sure to place it somewhere that doesn't matter or is easy to clean. I didn't find the machine all that difficult to clean after using but you have to have a little patience. Hold it upside down and use the garden hose on low flow to wash out the solution tray being careful not to wet the motor or switch.. We ran this off and on over the 3 day July 4th weekend and it ran perfectly. Kids and adults both were amazed. If you want a bubble machine and don't want to spend a lot of money get this one.

text_fidelity_a:
SYMA Mini Drones for Kids or Adults, Easy Indoor Flying Helicopter with Auto Hovering,3D Flip,Headless Pocket Quadcopters UFO Toy Gift for Boys Girls Disclaimer: I own a DJI Mavic Pro, and started out with a Holy Stone quadcopter. I've flown smaller ones like the DJI Spark and the DJI Tello, which is similar in size. I would say that for the price, this is a five-star drone. You get a lot for 35 dollars. Compared to other drones, I would say that there are certain improvements that could be made but those drones are much, much more expensive.
Pros:
Small manageable size - the drone is quite small, which is nice because it lends itself to indoor flight and easy travel. It is about 4.5 inches by 4.5 inches for a length and width, and the diagonal rotor distance is about 5 inches, while to entire copter stands at about 1.25 inches. This, as I said, is nice for indoor flight and you don't have to worry too much about hitting someone. You can also easily launch it and land it from and on your hand.

Robust and reasonably crash proof - The blade guards proved themselves quite useful, as I bumped it into walls several times, and the guards did their job. The copter simply bounced off the wall and continued flying. Additionally, when I was testing it, the drone died while flying. I knew this was coming, as I could feel the responsiveness beginning to slow and the flip function would no longer work. The drone fell from about 12 feet in the air onto the blacktop. I didn't notice and dings, dents, or scar=tches, and once it was charged, it flew fine.

Quiet - The drone has a shrill high pitched sound as it flies. It isn't too loud, and I could talk to those next to me while flying without having to raise my voice while the copter was only a few feet away.

Auto-flip function - This is fun. Executed, the drone flips in your specified direction, rolling quickly left, right, forward of backward and returning to hovering once completed. The flip function does not work once the battery drops below a certain percentage.

LED lights for battery and connectivity - These are easy to see when on the ground and display info about the battery when charging or low, and connectivity when first powered on. The rear lights are green, and the ones in the front are red, but they can be hard to see in daylight once it gets more than about 30 feet away.

Good range. I flew the drone about 70 or 80 feet away laterally without any problems, and about 40 feet up before coming down for fear of wind gusts. It worked fine, with no noticeable latency.

Headless Mode - Great function for learning pilots, especially for a drone like this that has no camera feed. However, the instructions are quite confusing on how to engage this and it took me a solid 5 minutes of fiddling with the controls to get it to work. To get this to work, take off, hold the button a the top left of the controller until it starts beeping, and then push the stick forward. The forward-facing direction will remain that relative forward until this function is disengaged.

Cons:
Disproportionate flight to charge time ratio - According to the user manual, this charge time is about 70 minutes, while the flight time is around 5 minutes while hovering. I, however, found that it took about 35 minutes (charging for a wall outlet) for a full charge from dropping out of the sky dead. The flight time that I got was about 6 minutes, doing maneuvers, flips, climbing, falling, accelerating and decelerating. Still, I think this could be improved, and, as there are no removable batteries you can plug in once another is dead, I make using the drone for more than 10 minutes hard.
Poor wind resistance - This thing blows outside with the slightest breeze. Inside, the flight trim is hard to adjust, and outside, it is not worth it. I found myself constantly adjusting to compensate for any wind.
Instructions aren't very clear - I found myself struggling to engage Headless mode, as well as find things within the manual. There are occasional typos, and the layout is confusing.
Joysticks don't articulate much - This is actually somewhat annoying. there isn't much height to the sticks, and they don't move around much, making any more precise movements difficult. Additionally, the other buttons on the controller are somewhat difficult to press.

I liked this drone, especially for the price. This would be great for any kid, or even as a starting copter for someone who wants to see if they are interested in them. I like the size, durability, and flip function, but the battery life and wind resistance are something to consider.
text_fidelity_b: SYMA Mini Drones for Kids or Adults, Easy Indoor Flying Helicopter with Auto Hovering,3D Flip,Headless Pocket Quadcopters UFO Toy Gift for Boys Girls

Overall PROs- cute felt pieces that easily attach much like a button hole that toddler can practice with.
CONs-cheap plastic sewn mat, hard to attach buttons, useless strings, mat falling apart during first play.

text_fidelity_a: Faber-Castell Do-Art Dot a Design Animals For ages 6 and up. The set comes with 6 "design sheets" for kids to paint, but there are only 3 designs (koala, turtle, or dolphin). You get one sheet with only black-and-white lines for an older child to paint and dot. You also get that same design with the main colors pre-printed and you only need to add dots of paint to the white dots in the design. The kit also comes with: 8 acrylic paints (light blue, dark blue, green, yellow-green, yellow, orange, red, purple), 2 fine tip dotters, 1 medium tip dotter, 1 brush, sticky tac (keeps paper flat while painting), 2 cardboard frames with hangers, and instructions. Acrylic paints can dry out quickly, so you may need to add water to the paints to keep them from drying out. Acrylic paints can quickly dry onto clothing and not come out, so you'll want to wear a painting smock. Wash dotters, brush (and work surface) before the paint dries if you intend to reuse them. The "dotters" are foam rounds on the end of a handle, and they create somewhat raised paint dots on the design sheets. It's a fun idea with colorful paints, but it is kind of simple so probably for younger kids rather than teenagers or older.
text_fidelity_b: Faber-Castell Do-Art Dot a Design Animals

Olefun Sight Words Flash Cards with Characters Scene & Motion & Sentences-220 Educational Flash cards for Age of 4,5,6,7 Years old,Pre K,Preschool, Kindergarten,1st,2nd Grade,Homeschool,Learn to Read. These Sight Words cards are great overall. I especially like that multiple levels come in one box, so it can work great for multiple ages in one home, or grow with a single child for several years. We are at level 1, so we will get a lot of use from this set.

Using the cards, I show my child an image with a word on the front side, and then I have notes on the backside for each word. I improvise a lot with these cards by asking my child to do different things that I think make more sense for the room we’re playing in, but sometimes I also use the suggestions on the back. We think it’s fun, and it’s a great learning opportunity to become familiar with how sight words look, while playing by acting out what the words mean.

One observation that struck me as odd is the text for the letter K. I do not believe children are taught to read or write this letter in this format, so I feel it is an odd choice. Otherwise, this kit is a great learning tool for kids!

4 cubes butter, softened
2 heaping cups dark brown sugar (packed, then heap that shiz)
½ cups white sugar
2 tablespoons vanilla
1 ½ teaspoon salt
1 ½ teaspoons baking soda
3 eggs
6 cups flour
1 bag chocolate chips (semi-sweet or sweet)

Mix BY HAND all ingredients, except flour and chips (mixing by hand makes them taste better, trust me).
Then add flour and chips and stir BY HAND. Bake @ 350 for 9-11 minutes on ungreased cookie sheet. Enjoy the preciouses.
Note: makes a buttload of cookies, so you might want to halve the recipe.

text_fidelity_a:
Oltree | Cooperative Strategy Game for Teens and Adults | Ages 8+ | 2 to 4 Players | 60 Minutes Oltree is a cooperative board game based off of a French role playing game of the same name. I haven't heard of that game, but it's vaguely King Arthur-themed, and reeks of middle age knights and peasants stuff, minus the dragons.

I get the feeling that these are well-known characters in that universe, and I think that if you know who they are, that might add an extra layer of fun to the game. As it is, this game is very...dull. It has a story, and that story is quite predictable, and you'll end up replaying the same ten scenarios over again if you complete the campaign. The writing wasn't exactly bad, but nothing really stood out amongst any of the cards. The actions are largely mechanical, but it is fun the first few times you work to add a barracks to your castle or help a damsel in distress.

I will say that the best element of the game is the production value. This is the only version of this game (that I know of) and it feels like what you'd get from a $100+ Kickstarter campaign, with wooden everything and quality cards.

I think if the characters provided a bit more personality to the story, or if I knew something more about the world, I might really like this game, but I found it rather mechanical and slow moving, and the campaign didn't hook me as well as I'd hoped. It's not a bad game, but it wasn't for me.
text_fidelity_b: Oltree | Cooperative Strategy Game for Teens and Adults | Ages 8+ | 2 to 4 Players | 60 Minutes

Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer, Outdoor Toy for Kids Ages 3-7, Red Toddler Bike Coming from a family of mostly boys and Big Wheel lovers, I know these current low riding Big Wheels are not the same quality as my little brother's Big Wheel from 1971. My brother loved his Big Wheel so much, that my son also had to have one when he was 3. Even though he was too small, he didn't care- walking it was just as good as riding it.

Things haven't changed much in the design, the big wheel bikes are all still too large for children under 4-5, but the quality has changed a lot for the original Big Wheel. After replacing the back seat 3 times, the original current Big Wheel of our nephew's recently went to the garbage. Replacing the Big Wheel with a tricycle was even worse- after a couple turns- the head injuries even with a helmet proved to be going from a cheap big wheel to bruises.

This Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer is very similar to the Big Wheel of the seventies- very sturdy. The seat doesn't break at the pegs like the current Big Wheel. It is still too large for children under 5, but they don't care- they enjoy just having it, even if they have to walk it. They use their feet anyway for braking, so they don't mind walking it until their feet reach the pedals. My son walked his Big Wheel for a year before he could reach the pedals.

The best thing about this Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer is our nephews love it. Taking the fastest high speed turns ends up in falls inches from the ground- meaning less painful minor injuries. My brother and son never had a bad injury being so close to the ground and this was in the days of no head protection. Putting it together was not difficult with the directions and once together, it's hard to keep the kids off. It's nice to see Radio Flyer keeping the tradition of making a sturdy Big Flyer that is perfect for 4 to 7 year olds, just like in the seventies when things were built to last.
text_fidelity_b: Radio Flyer Deluxe Big Flyer, Outdoor Toy for Kids Ages 3-7, Red Toddler Bike

LeapFrog LeapReader Deluxe Writing Workbook: Learn to Write Letters with Mr. Pencil The letters in this book aren't done in order. If you're wanting this book to teach letters, that might be important to know. I've chosen to teach in order, and am working on that with my two oldest. (I know some teach letters out of order, which is great, too) Either way, with this book they're learning letters. Plus, there's an alphabet chart on the last page that does put the letters in the correct order. It seems as though the letters in this book are introduced according to how easy they are to write(straight lines, curves, etc). So, as your child goes along, the letters get harder and harder to write.

Also, both uppercase and lowercase letters are included in this book.

Each page in the book has a little practice sheet. These sheets are super sensitive to pressure. Any pressure at all from any source, and a "pencil" mark will show up where you've written. Once you've used these sheets, they are useless. (You can't erase) You are provided with an extra set of sheets, and given the warning to NOT stack and to separate them before writing. When your little one is done with the sheets, they can be easily torn out, and the book will work perfectly fine without them. Your child can still practice "writing" letters just using the book.

Since music is an important part of this book's story, I enjoyed that added lesson for my little ones. There's even a piano included that can be played, which makes me like this book even more.

Overall, this is a wonderful tool to have for learning! I'm looking forward to adding the numbers book to our library soon!
text_fidelity_b: LeapFrog LeapReader Deluxe Writing Workbook: Learn to Write Letters with Mr. Pencil

Feleph Jungle Trees Building Blocks Bricks with 2 Base Plates (10 Inches for Each), Forest Garden Plants Flowers Bushes Animals Kit, Botanical Parts Scenery Toys Compatible with Major Brands LEGO would never make something like this. Sure, you can take their stuff and make anything with them, but too many of their kits make a definitive something. This is a definitive nothing, but a nothing that can entertain far beyond what a lot of different "somethings" can do.

LEGO is a toy, and this is often something that they remember to a fault. Here is a LEGO competitor, with bricks that are compatible, that remembers that it's not always a toy that kids want. They want an experience of playing, and that's what this Forest Garden kit gives them. Is it a dinosaur jungle? Is it a very nice tropical garden? Are the characters running from that alligator, or picnicing i the woods? With this, more than with any LEGO kit I've ever reviewed, there is a limitless number of possibilities.

There are no instructions with this kit, which is somewhat bothersome for the finnicky children who need a "right" way to put them together, but the playscape this provides is so unique that I can't give it less than 5 stars.

Disney Sorcerer's Arena: Epic Alliances Core Set | Strategy Board Game for 2 or 4 Players Ages 13 & Up | Featuring Disney and Pixar Characters & Villains | Officially-Licensed Family Game If there was one company I can confidently say I wouldn't have expected a skirmish miniature battle game to come from, it would be a Disney mashup. Ariel and Aladdin get out there and trade punches with Gaston? I wouldn't have thought.

But that's exactly what you have here. The character mashup is novel, and the board, pieces and cards are pretty good quality, although I am not a fan of the poorly implemented version of the "Heroclix" format you see on these acrylic minis. They look good, they're just a bit difficult to fiddle with.

The game is broken into chapters, and you can really start exploring the entire set starting with Chapter 2 rules, which are a good starting point for experienced gamers and older children as well.

I'm excited to see what could come from the expansions for this game and which characters they choose to add. I don't think there are going to be a lot of people who gravitate towards Dr. Facilier, for example, so some more fan favorites would be nice to see.

Generally speaking, I really like this game and I think it will make for a fun tactical combat game for people of any age to enjoy.
text_fidelity_b: Disney Sorcerer's Arena: Epic Alliances Core Set | Strategy Board Game for 2 or 4 Players Ages 13 & Up | Featuring Disney and Pixar Characters & Villains | Officially-Licensed Family Game

text_fidelity_a: Doggie Doo Corgi Game - Unpredictable Action - Feed The Doggie and Collect His Doo to Win - Includes 24-Piece Puzzle by Goliath This type of thing isn't usually my cup of tea and I typically dislike potty humor. This looked like something to bring humor on the days that my guys aren't getting along, though. It is on the weird side(even thought so from my 3 boys), with all the noises, but it is also on the humorous side. To play, you stick a bit of slime("food") into the bone. The players take turns rolling the die and squeezing the bone the amount rolled. Each player has a shovel that they place behind the dog to catch the "doos" before squeezing the bone. Each time the dog poos, you have to refill the bone. Once all the slime is gone, the player with the most "doos" wins. Had I known that the game used slime, I never would have gotten it. I've had to throw out too many items ruined from it to want it in my home anymore. We just try to be extra careful when playing. It comes with two bags, but it only takes one to play. The second bag is for if the first gets ruined. It says on the bag that it's non-toxic, but to still wash hands after touching it. When the game works, it's fun and makes us laugh. We've had lots of trouble getting it to work properly, though. Many times it won't seal just right(I guess) and no amount of squeezing the bone will make anything happen. It warns not to put too much, which we've tried not to do, and to also make sure the bone is pushed all the way in, which we've tried to do. It still won't work for us half the time, though, which makes it frustrating. If the slime ever gets stuck, the game does come with a stick to push it out. It also comes with a puzzle, which is a nice bonus. Overall, it's still a fun game.
